# Compu Methods

<!-- purpose: Where Compu Methods files live, the kinds they hold and every key they accept -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

Computation methods, one file each under `data_types/compu_methods/`: how a stored value becomes the physical or the named one, an element a type names by reference. Two element kinds discriminated by `kind` (`texttable`, `linear`), plus one nested member kind (`table_entry`). An enumeration, a value type and a reference type name a `texttable` by their `compu_method_ref`, an application type names a `linear` by its own. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.

One file per `compu_method`, in `data_types/compu_methods/` under the model root, named after its `name` and ending in `.yaml`. Where that file name is already taken by another element's file — compared without regard to case — the file gets the nearest free `~1`, `~2`, … instead; the element is identified by the `name` inside the file, never by its file name.

A file of this layer is one of 2 kinds — `texttable`, `linear` — chosen by its `kind` key.

## `texttable` { #texttable }

<!-- purpose: Writing `texttable` files in Compu Methods: each key, its type and default -->

A computation method of category `TEXTTABLE`, emitted as a `COMPU-METHOD` in `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`: a table of named values, one closed single-point `COMPU-SCALE` per entry, the shape an enumeration's own generated method has. An enumeration names one by its `compu_method_ref` in place of inline `literals`, and an implementation value or reference type by its `compu_method_ref`, which is the one way an implementation type states literals.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The compu method's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/compu_methods/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the compu methods, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name. |
| `kind` | string, one of `texttable` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this compu method kind; always `texttable`. |
| `entries` | a list of `table_entry` blocks | yes | — | The table's named values, addressed by `name`, in the order they are emitted. Must not be empty: a `TEXTTABLE` holds one or more scales. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the compu method. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`, its layer's package, this compu method is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the compu method and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/CompuMethods/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/CompuMethods` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |

## `linear` { #linear }

<!-- purpose: Writing `linear` files in Compu Methods: each key, its type and default -->

A computation method of category `LINEAR`, emitted as a `COMPU-METHOD` in `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`: physical = stored × `factor` + `offset`, one `COMPU-SCALE` in the internal-to-physical direction, referring to the `unit` element it names. An application type names one by its `compu_method_ref`, in place of an inline `conversion`. It holds no scale label, which the standard makes not applicable for a `LINEAR` scale; the scale's limits are its optional `limits`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The compu method's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/compu_methods/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the compu methods, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name. |
| `kind` | string, one of `linear` | yes | — | The discriminator that selects this compu method kind; always `linear`. |
| `unit` | string, the `name` of [units](units.md) | yes | — | The name of the declared unit, an element of the `units` layer, the method refers to: a `LINEAR` computation method refers to a unit. Must not be blank. |
| `factor` | number | no | `1.0` | The multiplier applied to the stored value. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float. |
| `offset` | number | no | `0.0` | The constant added after the multiplication. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float. |
| `limits` | a `linear_limits` block | no | absent | The limits of the linear computation method's scale, on the stored side: the values the conversion is defined for, which is what the standard reads a scale's limits as -- the limiting values before the conversion is applied. Written as the scale's `LOWER-LIMIT` and `UPPER-LIMIT`. Absent, the scale states no limit and the conversion applies to every stored value; it is not the physical range, which is the type's `range`. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the compu method. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
| `package` | string | no | absent | The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`, its layer's package, this compu method is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the compu method and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/CompuMethods/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/CompuMethods` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule. |

## Blocks used inside those files { #blocks-used-inside-those-files }

<!-- purpose: The blocks nested inside Compu Methods files, which are not files of their own -->

These are not files of their own: each appears as a block inside an element of this layer.

### `linear_limits` { #linear_limits }

<!-- purpose: Writing `linear_limits` blocks in Compu Methods: each key, its type and default -->

The limits of a linear computation method's scale, on the stored side. A nested object rather than a list member, so it has no identity of its own and every field of it may change. Either limit may be left out; the lower one must not be above the upper one, and the two may be equal only when both are closed.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lower` | a `linear_limit_bound` block | no | absent | The lowest stored value the conversion applies to, written as the scale's `LOWER-LIMIT`; omitted or `null` when the scale states none. An infinite limit is no bound: leave it out. |
| `upper` | a `linear_limit_bound` block | no | absent | The highest stored value the conversion applies to, written as the scale's `UPPER-LIMIT`; omitted or `null` when the scale states none. An infinite limit is no bound: leave it out. |

### `linear_limit_bound` { #linear_limit_bound }

<!-- purpose: Writing `linear_limit_bound` blocks in Compu Methods: each key, its type and default -->

One limit of a scale: a stored value and whether the limit itself belongs to the interval. A nested object rather than a list member, so it has no identity of its own and every field of it may change.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | number | yes | — | The limit's stored value. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float; it accepts neither NaN nor ±Infinity. |
| `interval` | string, one of `closed`, `open` | no | `closed` | Whether the limit belongs to the interval: `closed` (it does; the default, as an absent `INTERVAL-TYPE` is) or `open` (it does not). Written as the limit's `INTERVAL-TYPE`. |

### `table_entry` { #table_entry }

<!-- purpose: Writing `table_entry` blocks in Compu Methods: each key, its type and default -->

One named value of a `texttable`: a member of its `entries` collection, never a standalone element, so it has no file and no layer-level address. It has an enum literal's shape.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The entry's identity inside its table, written as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `SHORT-LABEL` and its `VT`, exactly as an enum literal's name; must not be blank, and immutable. |
| `value` | integer | yes | — | The integer the entry stands for, emitted as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `LOWER-LIMIT` and `UPPER-LIMIT`. |
| `description` | string | no | `""` | Free text about the entry. Written into the generated ARXML as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none. |
